# Ezekiel 8 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** In the sixth year of exile, on the fifth day of the sixth month, I was sitting in my house with the leaders of Judah sitting in front of me, when the power of the Lord GOD suddenly came over me.

**2** I looked and saw a figure that appeared to be made of fire — from the waist down, all fire; from the waist up, glowing like bright amber.

**3** He reached out what looked like a hand, grabbed me by the hair, and the Spirit lifted me into the air between heaven and earth. In a vision from God, He transported me to Jerusalem — to the entrance of the north gate of the inner court, where a disgusting idol that provoked God's jealousy had been set up.

**4** And there I saw the glory of the God of Israel, just as I had seen it in my vision in the valley.

**5** "Son of man," He said, "look toward the north." I looked, and there at the entrance north of the altar gate stood this idol that provoked God's jealousy.

**6** He said, "Son of man, do you see what they're doing? The people of Israel are committing horrible sins here that are driving Me away from My own Temple. But you're about to see even worse."

**7** He brought me to the entrance of the courtyard, and I could see a hole in the wall.

**8** "Dig through the wall, son of man," He said. So I dug through, and found a hidden doorway.

**9** "Go in," He said, "and see the sickening things they're doing in there."

**10** So I went in and looked — and there on the walls all around were carvings of every kind of crawling creature and disgusting animal, along with all the idols of Israel.

**11** Standing in front of these images were seventy of Israel's leaders, including Jaazaniah son of Shaphan. Each one was holding an incense burner, and clouds of incense smoke were rising up.

**12** "Do you see this, son of man?" He asked. "Do you see what Israel's leaders are doing in the dark, each one in his private idol room? They tell themselves, 'The LORD can't see us. The LORD has abandoned the land.'"

**13** "But wait," He said. "You're about to see even worse."

**14** He brought me to the entrance of the north gate of the LORD's Temple, and there sat women weeping for the pagan god Tammuz.

**15** "Do you see this, son of man?" He asked. "You'll see things even more detestable than this."

**16** Then He brought me into the inner courtyard of the LORD's Temple. There, between the entrance and the altar, stood about twenty-five men with their backs turned to the LORD's Temple, facing east and bowing down to worship the sun.

**17** He said to me, "Do you see this, son of man? Isn't it bad enough that the people of Judah are committing these disgusting sins here? They've also filled the land with violence and are constantly provoking Me. Look — they're even holding branches up to their noses in pagan ritual!

**18** So I will respond in fury. I will show no pity and no mercy. Even if they scream to Me for help, I will not listen."

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

- **8:6**: God takes Ezekiel on a tour of horrors — showing him layer after layer of corruption in the very Temple that was supposed to be God's home. It's like walking through a crime scene with the homeowner.

- **8:12**: The leaders' excuse is chilling: 'God can't see us. God has left.' When people convince themselves God isn't watching, there's no limit to what they'll do — even in His own house.

- **8:16**: Priests with their backs to the Temple, bowing to the sun — this is the ultimate insult. They're literally turning their backs on God in His own sanctuary. No wonder He responds with fury.

— PNEUMA
